'''''Aglaonema modestum''''', called '''Chinese evergreen''', '''green-for-ten-thousand-years''', and '''lily of China''', is a species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Aglaonema]]'', native to Bangladesh, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, and southeast and south-central China.<ref name="84081-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:84081-1 |title=''Aglaonema modestum'' Schott ex Engl. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=13 January 2021}}</ref> In these areas, it is found in tropical swamps and rainforests.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Plants & Flowers » ''Aglaonema modestum'' |url=https://www.plantsrescue.com/aglaonema-modestum |access-date=12 May 2021}}</ref> 

== Cultivation ==
It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Aglaonema modestum'' Chinese evergreen |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/707/i-Aglaonema-modestum-i/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |quote=Other common names; … green-for-ten-thousand-years, lily of China |access-date=13 January 2021}}</ref>

''A. modestum'' is typically {{cvt|1-3|ft|cm|order=flip|round=5}} tall and {{cvt|2-4|ft|cm|order=flip|round=5}} wide. It occasionally produces white spathe-and-spadix [[Flower|flowers]] that give way to oval-shaped, reddish [[Fruit|fruits]] that are {{cvt|1-3|in|mm|order=flip|round=5}} long.<ref name=":0" /> Its lance-shaped leaves measure {{cvt|8x4|in|mm|sigfig=1|order=flip}}, and are borne on {{cvt|12|in|mm|sigfig=1|order=flip}} stalks that arise from a central growing point.<ref name=":1" />

''A. modestum'' requires a shaded location, and should not be exposed to temperatures below {{cvt|45|F|C|order=flip}}, which can damage the foliage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FPS25/FP025: ''Aglaonema modestum'' Chinese Evergreen |url=https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/FP025 |access-date=12 May 2021 |website=edis.ifas.ufl.edu |language=en}}</ref> It cannot endure direct sunlight and is a good choice for dimly lit rooms. It requires ample moisture except for a very short winter rest period, in which watering can be somewhat reduced. Young plants should be repotted every spring, while mature specimens need be repotted only every two to three years.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Chiusoli |first1=Alessandro |last2=Boriani |first2=Luisa Maria |title=Simon & Schuster's guide to houseplants |date=1986 |publisher=Simon and Schuster |location=New York |isbn=0671631314}}</ref>

== Toxicity ==
This plant contains [[calcium oxalate]] crystals which are poisonous to humans, dogs, cats, and horses. If ingested, it may cause severe burning and swelling in the mouth and tongue. Contact with the sap may also cause skin irritation.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=''Aglaonema modestum'' (Chinese Evergreen) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/aglaonema-modestum |access-date=12 May 2021 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref>
